'''Richard Alexis Zann''' (27 November 1944 – 7 February 2009)<ref name=Obituary>Clarke, Mike (2009) [https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1071/MUv109n2_OB "Obituary: Richard A. Zann, 27 November 1944–7 February 2009"] ''Emu'', '''109'''(2): 179-179.</ref> was an Australian [[ornithologist]].

==Early life and career==
Zann was born on 27 November 1944, and grew up in the town of [[Casino, New South Wales]], where he developed a boyhood interest in wildlife.<ref name=Obituary/> He graduated from the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]] in 1965, with a First Class Honours degree. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1972 at the [[University of Queensland]], studying the behaviour of [[Estrildidae|grassfinches]] under the supervision of [[Jiro Kikkawa]].<ref name=thesis/><ref name=Obituary/> He moved to [[La Trobe University]] in [[Melbourne, Victoria]] in 1972, where he remained until his death in 2009.<ref name=Obituary/>

The main focus of Zann's ornithological research was the [[zebra finch]].<ref name=Obituary/> This work was synthesised in the 1996 book ''Zebra Finch: A Synthesis of Field and Laboratory Studies'', which has been described as his [[magnum opus]].<ref name=Obituary/> Zann was also known for his studies on the [[island biogeography]] of the volcanic island of [[Krakatau]], [[Indonesia]].<ref>Anon. (1998). D.L. Serventy Medal 1998: Citation. Richard Alexis Zann. ''[[Emu (journal)|Emu]]'' 98: 242.</ref><ref>Robin, Libby. (2001). ''The Flight of the Emu: a hundred years of Australian ornithology 1901-2001''. Carlton, Vic. Melbourne University Press. {{ISBN|0-522-84987-3}}</ref> Zann was killed, along with his wife Eileen and daughter Eva, at [[Kinglake, Victoria]] in the [[2009 Victorian bushfires]].<ref name=Obituary/><ref>{{cite news |last=Vallejo |first=Justin |title=Loving families wiped out by an indiscriminate inferno |date=11 February 2009 |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0,22049,25037368-5013122,00.html}}{{dead link|date=October 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Honours==
In 1998, Zann was awarded the [[D. L. Serventy Medal]] by the [[Royal Australasian Ornithologists Union]] for outstanding published work on birds in the [[Australasia]]n region.<ref name=Emu/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://home.vicnet.net.au/_donvrac/news.html|title=Friends of Sherbrooke Forest, Inc. Newsletter No. 122|last=Incoll|first=Jan|date=2009|website=webarchive.nla.gov.au|archive-url=https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20090821140100/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/46107/20090822-0001/home.vicnet.net.au/_donvrac/news.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2009-08-21|access-date=}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In an obituary published in 2009, colleague Mike Clarke described Zann as "a reserved, humble, self-effacing man with a particularly dry sense of humour, who often made fun of his own shortcomings."<ref name=Obituary/> In 2010, the scientific journal ''[[Emu (journal)|Emu]]'' published a special issue in Zann's memory, dedicated to the zebra finch.<ref name=Emu>Buchanan, Katherine L., Simon C. Griffith, and Sarah R. Pryke (2010) [https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1071/MUv110n3_PR "The Zebra Finch: a synthesis revised"] ''Emu'' '''110'''(3): i-ii.</ref>
